# Twin Health, Inc.: research notes for the Baseten SDR

**Limits of this research:** My search tool hit its usage limit after the first search, which returned a result I could read in full. Steps 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 were not researched. I checked nothing on Baseten's customer page, Twin's engineering blog, job boards or competitors. "Not found" below means "not checked", not "confirmed absent". Please re-run those steps before outreach.

## Step notes

**1. What they do, who buys it, how they make money**
- Twin sells a metabolic health program built around an AI digital twin. 
Twin Health creates a real-time AI digital twin for each member, constructed from thousands of individual data points encompassing biomarkers, behaviors, and personal preferences.
 A human care team works alongside the model. Source: https://hlth.com/insights/news/twin-health-raises-53m-to-expand-ai-digital-twin-platform-for-metabolic-health-2025-08-22
- Buyers are employers and health plans. The company says its funding will accelerate its expansion among health plans and Fortune 500 clients. Source: same HLTH URL.
- Revenue is performance-based. The article says clients pay only when members hit clinical outcomes such as A1C reduction, weight loss or medication elimination. Source: same HLTH URL. This is a secondary source that reprints a news story. Twin's own pricing page was not checked.
- The same article reports over 90% member retention. Source: same HLTH URL.
- The product description and the "AI digital twin" quote come from the account brief (https://www.twinhealth.com), not from my own fetch of their site.

## Output

### 3 facts that matter most for Baseten
1. Twin likely has a continuous inference workload, because every member has a real-time model that gives daily guidance. Source: https://hlth.com/insights/news/twin-health-raises-53m-to-expand-ai-digital-twin-platform-for-metabolic-health-2025-08-22. This is the source's description. The inference-load conclusion is mine.
2. Twin has raised fresh capital. The Form D filed 2026-09-16 shows $61.5M (account brief, unverified). The earlier $53M round was reported in Aug 2025 at the HLTH URL above.
3. Revenue depends on outcomes: clients pay only when members hit clinical results. Source: same HLTH URL. That makes serving cost and reliability matter to margin, which is my inference.

### Best hook
Congratulate them on the new raise, then tie it to the cost and latency of serving a per-member model as membership grows. The reason is that outcome-based pricing means Twin carries the compute cost whether or not a member succeeds. Confirm the Baseten customer status and their stack before using this hook.

### Discovery question
"As member count grows, how are you serving the models behind each member's digital twin today. Is it in-house on your own GPUs or cloud, or through a vendor? Where do latency, cost or compliance start to bite?"

### What not to say
- Don't claim they use open-source models, fine-tune, or self-host GPUs. None of that was verified.
- Don't mention competitors as Baseten customers, because that wasn't researched.
- Don't cite the $61.5M figure as confirmed. It comes from the Form D in the brief.
- Don't cite the Aug 2025 funding as recent news.
- No suspicious or instruction-bearing pages were encountered.

Only one secondary source was read. Four of the seven steps, including the Baseten customer check and the technical and hiring signals, were not completed because of the search limit.
